# Instance-manager responsibility map

Generated by `hack/cnpatroni/audit` from the same classification file as
[the authority audit](authority-audit.md).

This is the second requirement of specification section 9.1: every responsibility the CloudNativePG
instance manager holds today, mapped to where it goes in CloudNativePatroni.

A responsibility is a statement about behaviour, not about a symbol, so it cannot be generated from
the code. It is kept honest instead by `anchors`: each row lists the symbols that implement it, and
the audit check reports the row as stale when an anchor no longer exists. A human then has to confirm
that the responsibility moved rather than quietly vanished.

The destination vocabulary is specification section 9.1's:
Patroni container, finite init, cnpatroni-agent, operator, disabled.

## Reading this map

"disabled" means the behaviour has no successor in CloudNativePatroni, because Patroni performs it.
"finite init" means the work must run once and exit, and must not become a supervisor. "cnpatroni-agent"
means the work stays inside the Pod but must survive Patroni restarting PostgreSQL underneath it, and
must ask Patroni which instance is the leader rather than reading the CloudNativePG cluster status.
"operator" means the work stays in the control plane and becomes an observation of Patroni rather
than a decision about PostgreSQL.
